¿Quién es Erika Kirk y por qué su llegada a la Junta de la Fuerza Aérea causa rechazo?
Erika Kirk, viuda del activista conservador Charlie Kirk, fue elegida por el presidente Donald Trump para formar parte de la Junta de Visitantes de la Academia de la Fuerza Aérea de Estados Unidos (USAFA por sus siglas en inglés) tomando el lugar de su esposo.
La Junta de Visitantes consta de 16 miembros encargados de supervisar la moral, la disciplina, el currículo, la instrucción, el equipamiento físico, los asuntos financieros, los métodos académicos y otros asuntos de la USAFA. Además, también tienen el rol de hacer recomendaciones al secretario de guerra (anteriormente secretario de defensa) y al presidente.
A partir del pasado 10 de marzo, Kirk apareció en la lista de los miembros de la Junta entre los nombres apuntados por Trump. La portavoz de la Casa Blanca Olivia Wales confirmó el rol de Kirk con USA TODAY en un comunicado asegurando que el presidente había tomado una “decisión perfecta” al nombrarla como parte de la Junta.
Continuando el legado de Charlie Kirk
Erika continuará con el legado de su esposo difunto, Charlie, quien sirvió en este puesto anteriormente, confirmó Wales. “Inspirando a no solo la nueva generación, pero millones en todo el mundo con su audaz fe cristiana, su defensa de la verdad y su profundo amor a la patria”, agregó la portavoz.
Mientras formaba parte de la Junta, Charlie pidió al personal de la USAFA detalles sobre cómo seguían las órdenes del presidente Trump sobre la teoría crítica de la raza y la diversidad, la equidad y la inclusió preguntando “cómo la Academia está garantizando el cumplimiento del cuerpo docente para asegurar que la USAFA no impulse la cosmovisión de opresión, la dinámica opresor/oprimido, la ideología antioccidental, antiamericana y de género”, según notas de la reunión del 7 de agosto.
También impulsó aceleración para renovar la capilla de la Academia, según un memorando que Doug Truax, director ejecutivo de la Restoration of America Foundation, dirigió a la Junta.
¿Por cuánto tiempo servirá Erika Kirk para USAFA?
Según un comunicado compartido con USA TODAY por la USAFA aseguran que ellos “no influyen en la selección de miembros” y que “de acuerdo con la ley federal, los nombramientos de la Junta son realizados de forma independiente por el Presidente de los Estados Unidos y los líderes del Congreso, tanto de la Cámara de Representantes como del Senado, y la Junta proporciona informes y recomendaciones al Secretario de Guerra y al Secretario de la Fuerza Aérea”.
En base a su selección por parte del presidente Trump, Kirk servirá para la Academia por al menos tres años hasta que un nuevo sucesor llegue.
Erika cuenta con una licenciatura en ciencias políticas y relaciones internacionales de Arizona State University (ASU), según su biografía. Antes de casarse con Charlie en 2021, Erika ganó Miss Arizona USA 2012 y obtuvo una maestría en derecho de la Facultad de Derecho de la Universidad Liberty en 2019.
Con su reciente nombramiento para USAFA, solo quedan dos puestos disponibles de los 16 para la Junta los cuales serán definidos por Trump y el líder de la minoría de la Cámara de Representantes.
Los reporteros de USA TODAY Jonathan Limehouse y Saleen Martin contribuyeron a este artículo.
Comunícate con la reportera Paula Soria por correo electrónico: paula.soriaaguilar@usatodayco.com

États-Unis : Donald Trump nomme la veuve de Charlie Kirk à un poste prestigieux, une partie des Maga se déchirent
Erika Kirk va remplacer son mari, tué lors d’une réunion publique en 2025, au conseil d’administration d’une école militaire de renom aux États-Unis. Sa nomination, sur ordre de Donald Trump, a donné lieu à une passe d’armes entre influenceuses d’extrême droite.
Une nomination discrète à un poste clé. Près de six mois après la mort de son mari, l’ultraconservateur Charlie Kirk tué par balle lors d’une réunion publique dans l’Utah en septembre 2025, Erika Kirk a été nommée par Donald Trump au conseil d’administration de l’US Air Force Academy, en remplacement de son époux.
Son nom figure désormais sur la liste des 16 membres, bien que le conseil n’ait pas communiqué officiellement sur sa nomination, indique le site américain The Hill. Selon The Guardian, ce conseil est chargé d’« examiner le moral, la discipline, les programmes, l’enseignement, les équipements, les finances, les méthodes pédagogiques et autres questions » relatives à ce centre de formation militaire de Colorado Springs.
La Maison-Blanche s’est réjouie d’un « choix parfait ». « Charlie Kirk a siégé avec fierté au conseil d’administration, inspirant non seulement la prochaine génération de militaires, mais aussi des millions de personnes à travers le monde par sa foi chrétienne inébranlable, sa défense de la vérité et son profond patriotisme, a déclaré Olivia Wales, porte-parole de la présidence américaine, dans un communiqué. Erika Kirk perpétuera son héritage et défendra avec conviction la force aérienne la plus prestigieuse de l’histoire, dont les pilotes assurent la sécurité, la force et la liberté de notre nation. »
Passe d’armes entre influenceuses d’extrême droite
Ce n’est pas la première fois que le président des États-Unis nomme un fidèle au sein de ce comité. Mais ce choix-là a suscité de vives réactions, même parmi les partisans du président Trump. Sur les réseaux sociaux, des internautes reprochent notamment à Erika Kirk, 37 ans, son expérience militaire nulle, quand bien même son mari Charlie ne pouvait se targuer d’un CV plus riche en la matière.
« Je suis désolé, mais être la veuve d’un mari influent ne vous qualifie pas pour conseiller le ministère de la Défense sur les normes de l’Air Force », écrit ainsi sur le réseau X Zach Costello, un activiste chrétien conservateur pro-Trump suivi par plusieurs centaines de milliers de personnes sur ses différentes plates-formes.
Toujours sur X, l’influenceuse conspirationniste Candace Owens, qui cible régulièrement l’épouse de Charlie Kirk, a quant à elle ironisé sur sa nomination. « C’est une veuve en deuil, nous n’avons donc pas le droit de nous demander ce qui la qualifie pour occuper un poste de conseillère auprès de notre ministère de la Défense. Tout cela est parfaitement normal et seules des personnes DÉMONIAQUES remettraient en question cette nomination », écrit-elle.
En réponse à ce message, Laura Loomer, une autre activiste d’extrême droite proche de Donald Trump et figure du mouvement Maga (Make America Great Again), l’a alors accusée de développer une nouvelle théorie du complot. « Tout n’est pas conspiration », écrit-elle sur le même réseau social. « Charlie a été nommé. Il est maintenant décédé, et pour lui rendre hommage, sa femme prend sa place », justifie-t-elle.
Des propos qui font écho à ceux du représentant républicain du Texas August Pfluger, qui siège au conseil d’administration de l’US Air Force Academy. « Erika est la personne idéale pour remplacer Charlie au sein du conseil d’administration et poursuivre son travail visant à inspirer la prochaine génération de militaires et à faire progresser l’Académie », a-t-il déclaré.
Erika Kirk sur les traces de son mari
En décembre dernier, Erika Kirk avait apporté son soutien au vice-président américain JD Vance pour la présidentielle de 2028. Depuis la mort de Charlie Kirk, elle a pris la tête de Turning Point USA, l’influente organisation de jeunesse de son défunt mari. Cette association politique américaine destinée aux jeunes a joué un rôle important dans la campagne électorale victorieuse de Donald Trump en 2024.
« Nous allons faire élire l’ami de mon mari, JD Vance, en tant que 48e président, de la manière la plus retentissante possible », avait-elle lancé, lors de l’AmericaFest, un rassemblement conservateur organisé par Turning Point USA, première édition depuis l’assassinat de son fondateur.
JD Vance était proche de Charlie Kirk avant qu’il ne soit assassiné en septembre 2025 sur un campus universitaire de l’Utah.

sources.news_title: Donald Trump Appoints Erika Kirk to Air Force Academy Board, a Position Once Held By Charlie Kirk | Just Jared: Celebrity News and Gossip
Donald Trump just quietly gave Erika Kirk a very rare position
sources.text:
Erika Kirk, the widow of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, has been appointed to the U.S. Air Force Academy’s Board of Visitors, replacing her late husband.
While the appointment has not been formally announced by the Air Force Academy or the White House, Kirk’s name now appears on the board’s official list of members on the U.S. Air Force Academy’s website.
The Board of Visitors is a 16-member panel that advises the secretary of defense on issues at the Air Force Academy, including morale, finances and academics. The board is required to submit an annual report on the institution.
Newsweek reached out to the White House via email for comment.
Why It Matters
Trump has moved quickly during his second term to reshape the boards of visitors at the nation’s military academies, appointing several political allies and conservative figures.
Erika Kirk’s appointment continues that pattern and places her in the same role previously held by her husband before his death.
The decision has drawn attention because the appointment was not publicly announced, and because it comes months after Charlie Kirk’s assassination, which shocked the conservative movement and led to a reshuffling of leadership at Turning Point USA.
What To Know
White House spokesperson Olivia Wales praised the appointment in a statement, saying Trump had "made the perfect choice" in naming Erika Kirk to the board.
The U.S. Air Force Academy is one of the nation’s five federal military service academies and trains cadets to become commissioned officers in the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Space Force.
Located just north of Colorado Springs, Colorado, the academy was established in 1954 and offers a four‑year undergraduate program that combines academics, military training, athletics and character development.
The Air Force Academy is overseen in part by the Board of Visitors, a 16‑member advisory panel made up of presidential appointees and members of Congress. The board provides recommendations to the secretary of defense and submits annual reports on the academy’s morale, finances and academic programs.
Charlie Kirk, co-founder of conservative group Turning Point USA, was appointed to the Air Force Academy’s Board of Visitors in March 2025 and attended one meeting before he was assassinated on September 10, 2025, while speaking at Utah Valley University.
Other members of the board include several lawmakers, among them Senator Markwayne Mullin of Oklahoma, Trump’s nominee for secretary of homeland security, as well as Senators Tommy Tuberville of Alabama, Kevin Cramer of North Dakota, Ted Budd of North Carolina and John Hickenlooper of Colorado.
What People Are Saying
White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said in a statement: "Charlie Kirk served proudly on the Board, inspiring not only the next generation of servicemembers, but millions around the world with his bold Christian faith, defense of the truth, and deep love of country. Erika Kirk will continue his legacy, and will be a fearless advocate for the most elite airpower force in the history of the world whose warriors keep our Nation safe, strong, and free."
A U.S. Air Force Academy Spokesperson told Newsweek: "The U.S. Air Force Academy thanks all members of the USAFA Board of Visitors for their service and commitment to our mission. Under statute, the institution does not influence or take a position on the selection of individual Board of Visitors members. In accordance with federal law, Board appointments are made independently by the President of the United States and Congressional leaders in both the House and Senate, and the Board provides reports and recommendations to the Secretary of War and Secretary of the Air Force."
What Happens Next
Since the death of her husband Charlie Kirk, Erika Kirk has taken over as CEO of Turning Point USA. Her appointment to the board places her in a formal advisory role at the Air Force Academy as the panel continues its oversight work.

Erika Kirk Air Force Board Appointment Sparks Backlash as Critics Question Her Qualifications
Conservative voices, including Candace Owens, slam Erika Kirk's appointment, questioning her suitability for the defense role
President Donald Trump has appointed Erika Kirk to the US Air Force Academy's Board of Visitors this week, filling the seat left by her late husband, Charlie Kirk.
The decision has sparked a heated debate across Washington and on social media about her lack of military or academic experience for such a high-level advisory role. Critics, including former allies, are now questioning whether the move is a meaningful tribute or simply an act of political nepotism.
At 37, Erika Kirk has been added to the 16-member board of visitors alongside several other supporters of US President Donald Trump. This panel is tasked with examining the Colorado Springs facility's internal operations, including its financial dealings, teaching standards, and the general conduct and wellbeing of its students.
Trump had originally selected Kirk's spouse for the committee a year ago, where he served until he was fatally shot during a presentation at Utah Valley University last September. Following that tragedy, the seat remained open until his widow was recently named as his successor.
Unannounced Update to the Board List
While the academy did not issue a formal statement regarding her promotion, news of the change broke on Tuesday through The Hill and other political outlets. Erika Kirk has already been added to the official roster as one of the president's five current designees, leaving just one remaining vacancy on the panel.
Alongside Kirk, the president chose other notable figures for the role, including Alabama's Republican senator Tommy Tuberville. Joining them is Dina Powell, who previously served as a deputy national security adviser for strategy during the initial Trump term.
Most of the remaining seats are filled by bipartisan members of Congress. This includes two Republican senators, Kevin Cramer of North Dakota and Oklahoma's Markwayne Mullin, both of whom were selected by Senate Majority Leader John Thune. Notably, Mullin was recently chosen by the president to lead the Department of Homeland Security, succeeding the dismissed secretary, Kristi Noem.
Backlash Over Erika Kirk's Qualifications
President Trump's decision to appoint Charlie Kirk's widow to the US Air Force Academy's Board of Visitors has drawn sharp criticism from a range of opponents. On Tuesday, conservative commentator Candace Owens joined the fray, openly questioning 'what the hell' qualifies Erika for such a role.
Like many others, Owens has strongly disapproved of the move, questioning whether Kirk has the necessary background for the role. In a post on X this Tuesday, she wrote: 'She's a grieving widow so we have no right to ask what the hell qualifies her to a position advising our Defense Department. This is all perfectly normal and only people who are DEMONIC would question this appointment.'
Loomer Dismisses 'Conspiracy' Theories
Laura Loomer, a far-right influencer and loyal Trump supporter, hit back at Candace Owens' remarks, insisting that 'not everything is a conspiracy.'
In a post on X, Loomer explained that before Charlie Kirk was assassinated last September, President Trump had already chosen him to serve on the Air Force Academy board. She argued that Erika is simply taking the seat to honour her late husband's memory, adding that the situation is straightforward rather than a hidden plot.
White House Issues Formal Confirmation
While the move was initially described as a 'quiet' choice by the president because it lacked an immediate public statement, the White House eventually confirmed the decision. In a later briefing, officials confirmed that Erika Kirk had indeed been appointed to the advisory role.
White House spokesperson Olivia Wales described Erika Kirk as the 'perfect choice' to take over from her late husband. She noted that Charlie Kirk had served the board with pride, motivating both future service members and millions of others through his firm Christian faith, commitment to the truth, and patriotism.
Wales added that Erika Kirk would uphold this legacy as a 'fearless advocate' for the global airpower force and the personnel who maintain the nation's security and freedom.

In March 2026, online users shared a claim that U.S. President Donald Trump appointed Turning Point USA CEO Erika Kirk, the widow of slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk, to serve as a member on the Air Force Academy Board of Visitors.

In short, this claim was true.
White House spokesperson Olivia Wales confirmed to Snopes via email that Trump selected Kirk to serve in the same board seat previously occupied by her husband, who was killed on the Utah Valley University campus during a speaking event on Sept. 10, 2025:
President Trump made the perfect choice in appointing Erika Kirk to the U.S. Air Force Academy Board of Visitors. Snopes contacted Turning Point USA by email to ask if it wished to comment on Erika Kirk's appointment to the board and will update this story if we receive further information.
Air Force Academy Board of Visitors' purpose
Congress established (archived) the Air Force Academy Board of Visitors in 1956. Then-President Dwight Eisenhower selected aviator Charles Lindbergh and others to serve with the inaugural committee.
The board is comprised of "six persons designated by the President," as well as members of the House and Senate, and others. 10 U.S.C. § 9455 (archived) states, "The persons designated by the President serve for three years each," and that at least two president-designated members must be academy graduates.
The same statute says the person who appointed a member retains the power to select a replacement in the event of a member's death or termination from the board. In other words, the statute granted Trump the right to choose Charlie Kirk's replacement, resulting in his selection of Erika Kirk.

The United States Air Force Academy Board of Visitors (often abbreviated as USAFA BoV or simply Board of Visitors) is an official federal advisory committee established by federal law under Title 10 U.S. Code § 9455.
It serves as an independent oversight and advisory body for the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA) in Colorado Springs, Colorado.
The Board provides independent advice and recommendations to the Secretary of Defense (through the Secretary of the Air Force) and to the Armed Services Committees of the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives.

Morale, discipline, and social climate
Curriculum and instruction
Physical equipment and infrastructure
Fiscal affairs (budget and resources)
Academic methods
Any other matters relating to the Academy that the Board chooses to consider
The Board visits the Academy (at least annually, with additional visits approved by the Secretary of the Air Force), observes programs, receives briefings, gathers information, and makes recommendations for improvements.
It prepares semiannual reports with its findings, views, and suggested actions.
These recommendations have historically influenced changes at the Academy, such as enhancements to training programs, emphasis on certain developmental areas (e.g., airmanship or leadership), performance assessments, infrastructure support, and more recent focuses like cadet enrollment levels, faculty audits, admissions processes, and facilities investments.
Membership is bipartisan and includes a mix of congressional leaders and appointees:
Six members appointed by the President
Designations from congressional leaders (e.g., Speaker of the House, Senate Majority Leader, chairs/ranking members of the Armed Services Committees, etc.)
Members serve without compensation (though travel and per diem may be reimbursed) and include U.S. Senators, Representatives, and other prominent citizens or experts.
The Board operates under a charter, bylaws, and the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) requirements, with meetings generally open to the public (except when closed for specific legal reasons).
